items.title: Milestone ledger brief by default
items.context: milestone_status and the appendMilestoneStatusAfterMutation() suffix (cli-engine.ts) that rides on story_advance and other mutating commands print a compact summary by default: per-milestone one-line status, counts, and next action. The full 7-column markdown table (renderMilestoneStatusReport in packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts) is available behind an explicit full-output flag.

happy.desc: Run lattice milestone_status for a story with populated milestones (no flags) -> output is a compact one-line-per-milestone summary (status, counts, next action) fitting under ~1k tokens; WHY: confirms brief default activates for milestone_status

Run lattice story_advance (or other mutating command that triggers appendMilestoneStatusAfterMutation) -> appended milestone suffix is the compact summary, not the full markdown table; WHY: confirms the mutation-suffix path also uses brief mode

Run lattice milestone_status --full (or equivalent full-output flag) -> output is the complete 7-column markdown table (renderMilestoneStatusReport); WHY: confirms full output is still accessible on demand

edge.desc: Run lattice milestone_status on a story with zero milestones -> output is empty/minimal and does not error; WHY: boundary: empty milestone set must not crash the brief renderer
Run lattice milestone_status on a story with >20 milestones -> brief output remains one-line-per-milestone without truncation loss of milestone identifiers; WHY: confirms scaling does not hide data

adversarial.desc: The brief milestone output still contains enough information for an agent to determine next action (i.e. identifies which milestone is current and what phase/checklist items remain); WHY: brief must not degrade agent decision-making

validate --full semantics remain untouched (validate is not in the affected command set) — confirm milestone_status full-output flag name does not collide with validate --full; WHY: per story constraint, validate --full must keep its run-real-machine-tests meaning

verificationEvidence.note: brief-output-smoke builds a fixture story with a populated milestone ledger and asserts the bare milestone_status default is the compact per-milestone summary under the byte budget; run green 2026-07-12 on post-commit HEAD.

milestone-status.test.mjs post-mutation blocks now assert the appended suffix: full 7-column table appears ONLY with LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 in env, proving the bare mutation suffix defaults to the compact summary (appendMilestoneStatusAfterMutation seam); brief-output-smoke also enforces the suffix budget.
Literal run on this story: emits the complete 7-column markdown table (three '| Milestone |' header rows incl. checklist-derived + closeout sections), 1,122 bytes vs 669 brief.
This story has zero milestones (ledger missing): brief renderer emits 669 bytes with Ledger: missing, Progress 0/0/0, Risks and an explicit Next action line; exit 0, no error.

Brief output preserves agent-actionable state: Phase, Progress counts (done/in-progress/not-started), current milestone status line, and an explicit 'Next action:' line naming the exact command; verified in the live transcript (Next action present) and asserted by brief-output-smoke.

validate is not in the brief-affected set: git diff HEAD~1 over packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts is empty (0 lines; file is in scope-contract explicitExcludes) and the validate schema in command-catalog is untouched, so milestone_status --full (declared per-command) cannot collide with validate --full run-real-machine-tests semantics.

items.title: finding_list brief by default
items.context: finding_list (packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts finding_list) defaults to one-liners: id, severity/category, status, evidenceState, truncated title. Full descriptions available behind the full-output flag. Explicit --json/--format=json machine mode keeps the current full shape.

happy.desc: Run lattice finding_list for a story with 3+ findings (no flags) -> output shows one-liner per finding: id, severity/category, status, evidenceState, truncated title; total output under ~2k tokens; WHY: confirms brief default for finding_list
Run lattice finding_list --full -> output shows full descriptions and all metadata fields for each finding; WHY: confirms full output accessible via explicit flag

Run lattice finding_list --json (or --format=json) -> output is the current full JSON shape unchanged: findings[] array with evidenceState field on each finding, plus attention.suspected array at top level; WHY: machine contract preservation per load-bearing context

edge.desc: Run lattice finding_list on a story with zero findings -> output is empty/minimal summary (e.g. No findings) without error; WHY: empty-set boundary

Internal consumer can JSON.parse bare finding_list output and read findings[].evidenceState and attention.suspected — verify the brief TEXT mode does NOT accidentally alter the JSON mode skeleton; WHY: load-bearing contract: internal callers depend on those fields

adversarial.desc: Run lattice finding_list with LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 env var set (no --full flag) -> output is full (env var overrides brief default); then add explicit --brief flag -> brief wins over env var; WHY: per-call flag beats env which beats default

Brief finding_list output still preserves finding id and evidenceState so an agent can decide whether to triage suspected vs verified findings; WHY: brief must not destroy decision-critical fields for agent-loop consumers

verificationEvidence.note: brief-output-smoke fixture has 3 findings; asserts bare finding_list keeps one entry per finding with id/severity/category/status/evidenceState + truncated title, drops heavy free-text, stays under budget, and sets _brief/_hint.
brief-output-smoke asserts finding_list --full restores the full metadata incl. the description spot marker.

brief-output-smoke asserts explicit --json finding_list key-set parity with brief env on/off: findings[].evidenceState per finding and top-level attention.suspected preserved in the unchanged full shape.
Zero-findings boundary on this story: bare finding_list returns the minimal JSON skeleton with an empty findings array and attention partitions; JSON.parse succeeds, exit 0.

evidence-state-gate-smoke JSON.parses BARE finding_list stdout and asserts attention.suspected is an array and evidenceState renders on every finding; green against the brief default, proving the skeleton contract holds.
brief-output-smoke precedence assertions: LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 with no flags renders full; adding --brief with env=0 still renders brief (flag wins).
Brief finding_list keeps id, severity, category, status and evidenceState on every finding (smoke skeleton assertion), so suspected-vs-verified triage remains possible without --full.

items.title: help brief by default
items.context: lattice help (packages/main/src/cli/help-renderer.ts printHelp) defaults to a compact catalog: grouped command names with short truncated descriptions, pointing at lattice <command> --help for details. Current verbose catalog available behind the full-output flag. Per-command --help output unchanged.

happy.desc: Run lattice help (no flags) -> output is a compact grouped catalog: command names with short one-line descriptions, ending with a pointer to lattice <command> --help; total output under ~3k tokens; WHY: confirms brief default for help
Run lattice help --full -> output is the current verbose help catalog with full parameter schemas and descriptions; WHY: confirms full output accessible on demand
Run lattice story_advance --help (any per-command help) -> output is unchanged from current behavior (not affected by brief mode); WHY: per story constraint, per-command --help output unchanged

edge.desc: Run lattice help when command list is empty or filtered to zero commands (e.g. in a phase with no allowed commands) -> output is graceful empty message; WHY: boundary: no commands should not crash
Run lattice help with a very long command registry (>100 commands) -> brief output still grouped and readable without truncation of command names; WHY: scaling boundary

adversarial.desc: Brief help output still contains every registered command name (no commands silently dropped) so an agent can discover available commands; WHY: brief must not hide capabilities from agent-loop discovery
The full-output flag for help does not collide with any existing help subcommand or flag semantics; WHY: no flag-name collision with existing help infrastructure

verificationEvidence.note: Bare help is 11,619 bytes (~2.9k tokens), grouped command names with short one-line descriptions and a footer pointing at lattice <command> --help and lattice help --full; budget probe (the story red-evidence command) now exits 0 (was 46,700 bytes red at baseline HEAD 0137b455).

verificationEvidence.command: bash -c 'test "$(LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 node bin/lattice.js help 2>/dev/null | wc -c)" -eq "$(node bin/lattice.js help --full 2>/dev/null | wc -c)"'
verificationEvidence.note: help --full emits the complete verbose catalog (45,481 bytes) byte-identical to the LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 output; probe compares the two byte counts for equality and passes.
cli-surface-smoke asserts per-command --help output (story_advance --help branding, owner-lease section) unchanged; printToolHelp untouched by the brief mode.

Brief help never drops command names: renderer truncates descriptions only (BRIEF_DESC_MAX) while every registered command name renders; cli-surface-smoke asserts host_runtime_list present on the BRIEF default and brief-output-smoke enforces the size budget with names intact.

The help --full/--brief flags are parsed at the help dispatch seam in cli-engine where no prior --full semantics existed; validate keeps its own --full untouched (diff over verifier.ts empty), and per-command --help flag handling is unchanged (cli-surface-smoke green).

items.title: Audit remaining >5k-token default outputs
items.context: Sweep other renderers/handlers whose default output exceeds ~5k tokens (~20KB) and apply the same brief-by-default pattern. Known from audit on 0.3.185: story_list default JSON dump 365KB, global bug_list 263KB, host_list 16KB borderline. Sweep method: rg for large markdown table builders and full-collection JSON returns in packages/main/src/handlers plus core renderers.

happy.desc: Run lattice story_list (no flags) -> output shows one line per non-terminal (actionable) story, with per-phase counts covering ALL stories including omitted terminal ones, under ~5k tokens on a 50+ story fixture; WHY: confirms brief default for story_list (known 365KB offender) with non-silent filtering

Run lattice bug_list (no flags) -> output is a brief summary: one line per bug with id, severity, status; total output under ~5k tokens for a project with 100+ bugs; WHY: confirms brief default for bug_list (known 263KB offender)
Run lattice story_list --full and lattice bug_list --full -> outputs are the current full JSON dumps; WHY: full output accessible on demand

Run lattice story_list --json -> output preserves _bugSummary field on each story object (internal consumers JSON.parse this); WHY: load-bearing contract: callers read _bugSummary from bare story_list output

edge.desc: Sweep confirms no other handler/renderer produces default output exceeding ~5k tokens (~20KB) that was missed; WHY: completeness of the audit (story says sweep method = rg for large table builders and full-collection JSON returns)
host_list (16KB borderline per audit) is either brought under brief-by-default or explicitly documented as acceptable; WHY: borderline case from the audit needs explicit resolution

adversarial.desc: Brief story_list output still includes enough skeleton that JSON.parse(output)._bugSummary is accessible (the brief JSON shape preserves the _bugSummary key even if other fields are omitted); WHY: internal consumer contract — callers read _bugSummary from bare story_list

Brief bug_list must not SILENTLY filter data: any omitted items must be represented by exact total/status counts and an explicit _hint naming the full flag, and --full must recover all omitted items; WHY: brief may filter to actionable subset only if non-silent and --full-recoverable

verificationEvidence.note: Live repo (234 stories incl. 187 DONE + 16 DISCARDED): bare story_list is 11,454 bytes (~2.9k tokens) with one-liners for non-terminal stories only, _phases counts covering ALL stories (non-silent), _brief/_omittedTerminal/_hint set; brief-output-smoke asserts the same on its fixture.

Bare global bug_list is 280 bytes on this repo: status counts cover all bugs, open bugs listed one-line each, _brief/_hint set; brief-output-smoke asserts one-liners + counts on its open/fixed fixture.

verificationEvidence.command: bash -c 'node bin/lattice.js story_list --full | wc -c && node bin/lattice.js bug_list --full | wc -c'
verificationEvidence.note: story_list --full emits the current full dump (119,866 bytes) and bug_list --full the full list (1,787 bytes); both restore the pre-change shape.

verify-story-list-bug-summary.mjs JSON.parses BARE story_list stdout and reads _bugSummary; green on the brief default (also fixed a pre-existing red: DISCARDED bug-stories no longer reported as unresolved).

Sweep completed with recorded method (wc -c over every read-only command on this repo + rg for table builders and full-collection JSON returns). Fixed in-story: story_list 119,866->11,454; bug_list 263KB-baseline->280; help 45,481->11,619; story_review 2,600,206->2,156; doctor 22,632->7,722; post-mutation milestone suffix. Audited under ~20KB threshold: checklist_get 19,502 (has slim), host_list 15,899, session_brief 6,479, status 1,421, recall 261, audit 496. Documented disposition: story_get 74,351 kept full-by-default because slim/fields is the sanctioned opt-in and CLAUDE.md requires full reads before evidence/mutations. brief-output-smoke enforces budgets on all fixed commands.

items.title: Escape hatch, JSON contract, and regression coverage
items.context: LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 environment variable restores full output as the default globally (per-call flag still wins). Explicit --json/--format=json outputs keep their current shape for machine consumers. Add a smoke test asserting brief defaults stay under a size budget, the full flag restores complete output, the env escape hatch works, and JSON opt-in shape is unchanged.

happy.desc: Set LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 env var and run any affected command (e.g. finding_list) without flags -> output is full (env hatch restores verbose default); WHY: confirms env escape hatch works
Set LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT=0 but also pass --brief flag -> output is brief (per-call flag wins over env); WHY: confirms precedence: flag > env > default

Run affected command with --json/--format=json -> JSON output shape is byte-for-byte identical to current production shape (same keys, same nesting); specifically: finding_list JSON has findings[].evidenceState and attention.suspected; story_list JSON has _bugSummary; WHY: machine contract regression test

Smoke test exists and passes: asserts brief defaults stay under a size budget (e.g. <5k tokens), full flag restores complete output, env escape hatch works, and JSON shape is unchanged; WHY: regression coverage as specified in checklist context

edge.desc: LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT set to empty string or non-0 value (e.g. 1, true, yes) -> brief default remains active (only literal 0 disables); WHY: env var parsing boundary

Existing internal callers (smoke tests, tasks) that shell out to affected commands or parse their stdout are audited and confirmed not broken by brief-mode default; WHY: initCheck issue flagged this — DEV must explicitly confirm no internal consumer parses brief text

adversarial.desc: validate --full is NOT affected by this change — running validate --full still means run-real-machine-tests, not show-full-output; WHY: story constraint: validate --full semantics must remain untouched

A command that does NOT have brief mode implemented (e.g. validate, checklist_get) ignores the LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT env and --brief flag gracefully (no crash, no behavior change); WHY: robustness — unaffected commands must not break if env var is globally set

The precedence chain (per-call flag > LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT env > brief default) is tested in a single test case with all three layers active simultaneously; WHY: confirms the layered override logic is correctly implemented

items.context: Documentation updates describing the new brief-by-default outputs, the per-command full-output flag, and the LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT escape hatch land in docs/CLI.md (and CLAUDE.md if the managed snippet regeneration applies). Satisfies scope-boundary allowed-item 6; verified by grepping the docs for LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT and the full-output flag.

happy.desc: rg for LATTICE_BRIEF_OUTPUT and the full-output flag name in docs/CLI.md -> both terms present and documented with brief-by-default behavior described, precedence rule stated (per-call flag > env > brief default), and affected command set listed; WHY: scope-boundary item 6 promises doc updates and this makes the promise verifiable

docs/CLI.md documents the frozen --json/--format=json contract (machine consumers get unchanged full shape regardless of brief mode); WHY: machine contract must be discoverable by integrators reading docs

edge.desc: docs list the exact set of affected commands (milestone_status, finding_list, help, story_list, bug_list, and any added by CHK-004 sweep) matching the actual implementation — no command listed that is not implemented, no implemented command missing from docs; WHY: docs-implementation consistency boundary
If CLAUDE.md managed snippet regeneration applies, the brief-mode behavior is also reflected there; otherwise docs/CLI.md alone suffices; WHY: CLAUDE.md is the agent-facing contract surface

adversarial.desc: Documentation does NOT promise any gate-behavior or gateEvidence semantics changes and does NOT claim validate --full changed meaning; WHY: story explicitly states no gate behavior change and validate --full semantics untouched — docs must not introduce false promises

Documentation does not claim brief mode affects --json/--format=json output shape — explicitly states JSON opt-in is unaffected; WHY: prevents future misinterpretation that could break machine consumers
